title: Custodian On‑Call Rotation, Evidence Ledger, and Status Templates
author: Ava Mitchell
content:
Overview

This document defines the "Custodian" on‑call model we use at Redwood: a structured rotation and succession practice focused on evidence collection, clean handoffs, and customer‑facing status messaging. It bundles: a concise incident process, an evidence ledger template, runbook excerpts, a postmortem rubric, a game‑day syllabus, and canned status/customer communications.

Why this exists
- Reduce time-to-evidence during incidents so SRE/engineers can move from triage to mitigation faster.
- Make handoffs deterministic (who owns what, and for how long).
- Standardize status messages to keep customers informed and to reduce cognitive load for responders.

Scope
- Applies to all Redwood production incidents affecting hosted inference, Dedicated pools, and Private deployments where Redwood provides operational support.
- Does NOT replace service-specific runbooks; it complements them with a universal evidence and handoff lifecycle.

Quick reference: severity & initial actions
1) Severity classification (fast reference)
   - Sev1 (SEV1) — total outage or widespread inability to create responses; immediate bridge, full responder mobilization.
   - Sev2 (SEV2) — significant degradation (latency/regressions affecting >20% of requests); bridge if escalation metrics hit.
   - Sev3 (SEV3) — localized or intermittent issues with limited customer impact.

2) First 10 minutes checklist (Custodian responsibilities)
   1. Acknowledge page and set status: acknowledge in PagerDuty/Slack and open incident doc.
   2. Record initial evidence snapshot into Evidence Ledger (see template below).
   3. Identify whether this is model quality, latency, capacity, or config failure. Tag incident type.
   4. If SEV1/SEV2, open a bridge and follow the Escalation Matrix.

Custodian rotation & succession policy
- Custodian role: the primary responder during the first hour of an incident. Responsible for evidence capture, triage summary, and handoff to remediation owners.
- Rotation cadence: custodians rotate weekly per team; schedule published in the SRE rota calendar.
- Succession rules:
  - If the custodian will be unavailable for >30 minutes, designate a successor immediately and update the ledger.
  - When escalating to a bridge, the custodian remains evidence owner until a bridge conductor is appointed.
  - After 60 minutes of active remediation, a formal handoff should occur (see Handoff checklist).
- Ownership timeboxing: custodians own the incident timeline for the first 60–120 minutes; long-term postmortem and action items are owned by the service steward.

Evidence Ledger (canonical entry schema)
- We require a single canonical artifact (the Evidence Ledger) per incident. The ledger is a short, human‑readable table captured in the incident doc with the following fields:
  - evidence_id: short token (e.g., EVID-20260112-03)
  - captured_by: responder name and role
  - timestamp_utc: ISO8601
  - snapshot_summary: 1–2 sentence summary of what was observed
  - artifacts: list of links to logs / traces / raw dumps (S3/Confluence/GCS IDs)
  - commands_run: exact CLI/HTTP commands used to capture snapshot (copy/paste)
  - retention_until: date after which artifact may be trimmed (per evidence retention policy)

Example ledger entry (plain-text table)
| evidence_id | captured_by | timestamp_utc       | snapshot_summary                          | artifacts                                       | commands_run                                   | retention_until |
| EVID-20260112-03 | Ava Mitchell | 2026-01-12T03:21:00Z | 30% of requests hitting 503 from model pool b | s3://redwood-evidence/2026/01/12/evid-03.tar.gz | curl -sS https://api.redwood.internal/health?pool=b > health.json | 2026-06-12 |

Minimum evidence capture (first 15 minutes)
- health check responses (JSON), 1m/5m graphs for availability, request traces (sample 10), router logs (last 30 minutes), recent deploys and rollouts.
- If model quality regression suspected: attach the failing prompt set and two golden responses.

Runbook excerpts (examples)
1) High latency (p90 > 2s and p99 > 10s)\   - Custodian: capture runtime metrics (nvidia-smi, dstat) and per-node latency histograms.\   - Command examples:
     - kubectl -n inference logs -l app=router --tail=200 | jq .latency | tail -n 50
     - curl -sS "https://metrics.internal/api/series?name=router.latency.p99&range=5m" | jq .
   - Quick mitigations: temporary route-weight shift to warm pools, increase batching window by 30ms, enable fallback model variant.
   - Escalation: if mitigation fails after 15 minutes, open an infra bridge and request capacity augmentation.

2) KV cache eviction storm
   - Custodian: identify eviction rate, affected model variants, and recent config changes to cache policies.
   - Evidence: include per-pod /proc/meminfo snapshot and runtime cache hit/miss metrics.
   - Mitigations: lower batch sizes, enable cache pinning for high-traffic prefixes, rollback recent cache policy change.

3) Model quality regression (semantic drift / hallucination spike)
   - Custodian: collect failing prompts, model version manifest, and differential eval against baseline.
   - Isolation: route traffic to previous model version variant; enable sampling for QA team.
   - Customer comms: notify impacted customers that we detected a model quality regression and have applied an immediate rollback for requests matching identified prompts.

Handoff checklist (formal handover after 60 minutes)
- Handoff note must be posted in the incident doc and include: brief timeline, canonical evidence id(s), current mitigations, open unknowns, and explicit next owner for remediation and postmortem actions.
- The following must be present before handoff: at least one artifact showing the root symptom, a mitigation plan or rollback trigger, and a named postmortem owner.

Postmortem rubric and timeline
- Postmortem required for all SEV1 and any SEV2 with customer impact.
- Timeline:
  - D+1: Incident triage summary and evidence ledger finalized.
  - D+3: Draft postmortem posted for peer review.
  - D+10: Postmortem finalized with action owners and acceptance criteria.
- Rubric (must be included in the postmortem):
  - Clear causal narrative (does the write-up explain why the root cause happened?).
  - Evidence linkage (do artifacts map to claims?).
  - Actionability (are there specific remediation actions with owners and deadlines?).
  - Learning (what monitoring/observability will change?).

Game‑day syllabus (2 hour canonical exercise)
- Audience: operators, SREs, serving runtime owners, product oncall reps.
- Objective: validate evidence capture, handoff, and customer messaging under time pressure.
- Schedule:
  - 00:00–00:15 — Briefing & objectives
  - 00:15–00:45 — Simulated incident: SEV2 latency spike; custodian captures evidence and opens ledger
  - 00:45–01:15 — Escalation to bridge; conduct bridge and perform mitigation (shift routing / rollback)
  - 01:15–01:45 — Handoff and write D+1 summary; begin a minimal postmortem draft
  - 01:45–02:00 — Retro: what artifacts were missing, communication friction points, and next steps to improve runbooks
- Grading checkpoints: evidence completeness score (0–5), handoff clarity (Y/N), status message accuracy (Y/N).

Status page & customer communications templates
- Principle: short, factual, and time‑boxed. Use the status page to report facts and the customer email for impact and remediation steps.

1) Status page message: Degraded performance (sample)\nTitle: Degraded performance for generation API in us-west-2
Summary: We are investigating higher-than-normal latency for the generation API affecting a subset of requests in us-west-2. We have identified increased queue times in router pool b and are applying routing adjustments to reduce customer impact.
Impact: Increased response times and occasional 503s for some customers in us-west-2.
Updated: 2026-01-12T04:03:00Z
Next update: 2026-01-12T04:18:00Z

2) Customer email (outage, templated)\nSubject: Redwood service disruption — Generation API degraded (Jan 12)
Hello [Customer name],

We experienced a disruption to the Generation API between 03:20 and 04:30 UTC on Jan 12 that may have affected some requests from your application. Root cause: an unexpected cache eviction pattern that caused routing congestion in a subset of Dedicated pools.

What we did: rolled back the cache policy change, shifted routing away from the affected pools, and deployed a mitigation patch to pin critical prefixes.
What we’re doing next: a postmortem will be shared by Jan 22; we have scheduled a permanent fix (ticket RW-3245) with an estimated completion by Feb 5.

If you saw user-facing errors or missing responses, please reply to this message and include sample request IDs so we can correlate with our evidence ledger.

Sincerely,
Redwood Support

Hardened status phrasing guidelines (short checklist)
- Avoid speculation. State facts and actions.
- Always include an ETA for the next update.
- Use plain language; avoid internal jargon unless targeted to platform customers who have agreed to technical notices.

Evidence retention and privacy notes
- Evidence artifacts are retained for 180 days by default, then truncated unless flagged for regulatory/enterprise retention.
- Redact PII before sharing artifacts externally; use the redaction tool documented in /confluence/security-and-compliance/redaction-tooling.

Appendix: useful commands and snippets
- Pull recent router logs (last hour) and save to S3:
  - kubectl -n inference logs -l app=router --since=1h > router-last-hour.log && aws s3 cp router-last-hour.log s3://redwood-evidence/$(date +%F)/router-last-hour.log
- Minimal evidence capture for model quality regression:
  - curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"<failing prompt>","limit":3}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" > failing-responses.json
  - tar -czvf evid-123.tar.gz failing-responses.json router-last-hour.log deploy-manifest.json

Governance and contacts
- Incident coach (rotation): list maintained in team calendar; reach out on #incidence-coach for mentorship.
- Evidence steward: security@redwood.com for guidance on retention and redaction.
